title: -ing as a subject: Swimming is fun
tagline: An -ing phrase can start a sentence and act like a noun, and it takes a singular verb.
why: When you talk about hobbies, habits and opinions, you need to start a sentence with an activity: Swimming is fun, Getting up early is hard. B1 Preliminary uses this pattern in the multiple-choice cloze and in the Writing email, and a speaker who can say Not eating breakfast is a bad idea sounds much more natural than one who only says I think it is bad to not eat.

hook.text: Sofia: "Swimming is fun!" Liam: "Getting up at six is not fun." Nadia: "Not trying is worse. Learning something new makes me happy."
hook.ask: Each sentence starts with a word ending in -ing. Is that word a person, a thing or an activity? And which verb comes next: is, is not, makes — one thing or many?

diagrams.title: Build the sentence with an -ing subject

watch_out.why: A base verb cannot be a subject. Use verb + -ing.

watch_out.wrong: Playing video games all day make you tired.
watch_out.right: Playing video games all day makes you tired.
watch_out.why: The -ing phrase is one subject, so the verb is singular: makes.

watch_out.wrong: Don't eating late is bad for you.
watch_out.right: Not eating late is bad for you.
watch_out.why: For the negative of an -ing subject we use not + -ing, not don't.
Use -ing alone, or to + base verb (To swim is fun), but never to + -ing.
After It's + adjective, we usually use to + base verb.
One activity, so one singular verb: is.

l1.why: Spanish uses the infinitive as a subject. English needs the -ing form.

l1.es: Fumar es malo para la salud.
l1.why: Again, Spanish infinitive becomes English -ing when it is the subject.
No eat does not exist in English. Use not + -ing.
English always needs a subject (It) and to + verb after the adjective.

remember.tip: When an activity starts the sentence, add -ing and then use one singular verb: Swimming is, Reading helps, Not eating makes.

dialogue.title: What makes a good weekend?
dialogue.context: Miss Vega asks Mateo, Sofia, Liam and Nadia what makes a good weekend during a quiet lesson.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: So, what makes a good weekend? Who wants to start?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: For me, sleeping late is the best part.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Really? Doing sport at the weekend makes me feel great.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I agree with both. Meeting friends is important, too.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Not having homework is the best thing for me!

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Ha! But doing your homework early gives you more free time.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: It's true. It's hard to start, but it feels good afterwards.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Finishing everything on Friday sounds impossible to me.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good point, Nadia. Talking about it is the first step!

can_do: I can start a sentence with an -ing phrase, like Swimming is fun.
I can use a singular verb after an -ing subject, even when the phrase is long.
I can make the negative with not + -ing and say the same idea with It's + adjective + to.
summary: An -ing phrase can be the subject of a sentence: Swimming is fun.
The verb after an -ing subject is singular: is, takes, makes, doesn't.
The negative is not + -ing: Not eating breakfast is a bad idea.
It's + adjective + to + base verb says the same idea: It's easy to make friends.
